problem: Changing the eviction test from `q[0] <= cutoff` to `q[0] < cutoff` silently moves the window from the documented `(now - window, now]` to `[now - window, now]`, so an entry at t still counts at now == t + window and `allow`/`remaining` give different answers from main there (steady one-per-window traffic gets half the throughput).

`retry_after` still returns `q[0] + window - now`, based on the old half-open window, so it returns 0.0 at t + window while `allow` refuses at that moment, and a client that follows it is rejected or loops on retries.

`setdefault(key, __import__("collections").deque())` bypasses the `deque` import on line 2 (ruff F401 now fails), allocates a throwaway deque on every call, and keeps the existing unbounded growth of `_accepted` from keys added by read-only calls.
There are no tests, and the comment documenting the window contract was deleted in the same change that altered the boundary, so nothing catches the now == t + window regression.

Pre-existing: a NaN `now` passes the monotonic check and is stored as `_last_now`, which permanently disables the time-went-backwards check and, once accepted, poisons the key (it is never evicted and `retry_after` returns nan).
Pre-existing: `_observe` stores `now` before checking it is a number, so one non-numeric `now` leaves the limiter raising TypeError on every later call.
Eviction uses `now - window` while `retry_after` uses `q[0] + window - now`, so with floats the two can round differently and disagree by one ulp at the boundary.
